subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In music production, 'multitracking' refers to...?
options: Playing many instruments live in one take with no overdubs
Compressing a stereo mix into mono
Recording different parts onto separate tracks so they can be balanced and edited independently
questions.explain: Multitracking records parts on separate tracks, allowing independent editing and mixing.

questions.q: A 'hook' in popular music is best described as...?
options: A modulation to the relative minor
A short, catchy musical idea designed to grab the listener and stick in the memory
A device for tuning the guitar
The final cadence of the song
questions.explain: A hook is a memorable, catchy idea engineered to capture and hold the listener's attention.

questions.q: 'Fusion' music is best defined as...?
options: A style that blends elements of two or more distinct traditions or genres
Music performed only on acoustic instruments
questions.explain: Fusion combines features of two or more traditions or genres, such as jazz-rock or Indian-Western fusion.

questions.q: In song structure terminology, a 'bridge' (or 'middle eight') typically functions to...?
options: End the song with a fade-out
State the main hook for the first time
Provide contrast in melody/harmony before returning to the chorus or verse
questions.explain: The bridge offers contrasting material that breaks up verse-chorus repetition before a return.

questions.q: Brahms is generally regarded as a Romantic composer who upheld which trait?
options: Classical formal structures within a Romantic idiom
questions.explain: Brahms combined Romantic expression with Classical forms such as the symphony and sonata, in the absolute-music tradition.

questions.q: Modal jazz, exemplified by Miles Davis's 'So What', is distinguished from bebop chiefly by its...?
options: Strict adherence to twelve-bar blues form
Use of static modes/scales held over long stretches rather than frequent chord changes
Reliance on rapid chord changes every two beats
questions.explain: Modal jazz bases improvisation on slow-moving modes held for many bars, freeing soloists from rapid chord changes.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the Brandenburg Concertos?
questions.explain: J. S. Bach composed the six Brandenburg Concertos, exemplars of the late Baroque concerto.

questions.q: An atonal passage is best characterised by which feature?
options: A clear tonic and dominant relationship
Strict adherence to a major scale
The absence of a tonal centre or key
questions.explain: Atonality avoids any sense of a key or tonal centre, abandoning functional harmony.

questions.q: In a typical pop or rock song, the section designed to be the most memorable and which usually contains the title and main hook is the...?
questions.explain: The chorus is the most memorable section, typically stating the title and main hook.

questions.q: A diminished seventh chord is built from which stacked intervals?
options: A major third and two minor thirds
questions.explain: The diminished seventh chord consists of three stacked minor thirds, dividing the octave symmetrically.

questions.q: Beethoven's symphonies are generally seen as bridging which two stylistic periods?
questions.explain: Beethoven extended Classical forms toward Romantic expression, bridging the two eras.

questions.q: Ragtime, popularised by Scott Joplin, is principally characterised by which rhythmic device?
options: A syncopated, off-beat melody set against a steady march-like bass
A swung shuffle feel in the bass
Rubato throughout with no fixed pulse
Continuous polyrhythmic layering of three rhythms
questions.explain: Ragtime sets a syncopated right-hand melody against a regular, march-style stride bass.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the 'tala' refers to...?
options: The cyclic rhythmic framework, a repeating cycle of beats
The melodic ornamentation of the soloist
questions.explain: Tala is the rhythmic cycle, a repeating pattern of beats that organises the music in time.

questions.q: The 32-bar 'AABA' song form, common in jazz standards, consists of...?
options: Four eight-bar sections where the third (B) provides a contrasting 'bridge'
A twelve-bar blues repeated until the soloist stops
questions.explain: AABA form has four eight-bar sections, with the B section serving as a contrasting bridge.

questions.q: Swing-era big bands such as Count Basie's typically organised their players into which sectional layout?
questions.explain: Big bands are built around a saxophone section, a brass section and a rhythm section.

questions.q: Gamelan ensembles commonly use which two tuning systems?
questions.explain: Gamelan typically uses the five-note slendro and the seven-note pelog tuning systems.

questions.q: Gamelan music frequently uses 'interlocking' (kotekan) parts, meaning...?
options: The ensemble plays in strict Western major scales
Two parts combine, each playing alternate notes, to create a single faster composite line
All players double the same melody an octave apart
questions.explain: Interlocking parts dovetail, each playing alternate notes so that together they form one rapid composite line.

questions.q: A recitative in Baroque opera primarily serves which function?
options: To advance the plot through speech-like singing
To display vocal virtuosity in an aria
questions.explain: Recitative uses a free, speech-like vocal style to carry the narrative between arias.

questions.q: In C major, the chord built on the leading note (vii) is which quality?
questions.explain: The triad on the leading note in a major key is diminished, comprising B-D-F in C major.

questions.q: The Latin American 'clave' is best described as...?
options: A characteristic two-bar rhythmic pattern underpinning many Afro-Cuban styles
questions.explain: The clave is a foundational two-bar rhythmic pattern that organises much Afro-Cuban and Latin music.

questions.q: The 'jhalla', the closing section of a North Indian raga performance, is characterised by...?
options: A fast, exciting climax with rapid rhythmic strumming
A return to the opening alap
Silence with only the drone sounding
A slow, free and unmetred mood
questions.explain: The jhalla is the fast, rhythmically exciting climax that ends the performance.

questions.q: In a major key, which chord built on the dominant typically functions as the dominant seventh?
options: A major seventh chord on the tonic
A minor seventh chord on the supertonic
A diminished seventh chord on the leading note
A major-minor (dominant) seventh chord on scale degree 5
questions.explain: The dominant seventh is a major-minor seventh chord built on the fifth degree, comprising a major triad plus a minor seventh.

questions.q: A ritornello in a Baroque concerto is which element?
options: A recurring orchestral refrain returning between solo episodes
questions.explain: Ritornello form alternates a recurring tutti theme (ritornello) with contrasting solo episodes.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.

questions.q: A melodic sequence is best described as which?
options: The simultaneous sounding of two melodies
The repetition of a melodic pattern at a different pitch level
A note held against changing harmony
The inversion of a melodic line
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic (or harmonic) idea successively higher or lower in pitch.

questions.q: The trio sonata of the Baroque is usually performed by how many players?
options: Four (two melody instruments plus continuo of two players)
questions.explain: Despite its name, a trio sonata's three written parts usually require four performers because the continuo bass is realised by a chordal instrument plus a bass instrument.

questions.q: Sonata form consists of which three main sections?
questions.explain: Sonata form unfolds in exposition, development and recapitulation, often with an introduction and coda.

questions.q: An appoggiatura is best defined as which?
options: A note approached and left by step
A dissonant note approached by leap and resolved by step
questions.explain: An appoggiatura is an accented non-harmony note usually approached by leap and resolved by step.

questions.q: Which jazz style, emerging in the 1940s, is defined by fast tempos, complex chord substitutions and virtuosic improvisation, associated with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie?
questions.explain: Bebop is the fast, harmonically complex and virtuosic jazz style pioneered by Parker and Gillespie.

questions.q: A passing note is which type of non-chord tone?
options: Approached and left by step in the same direction filling a melodic gap
A sustained dissonance held over a barline
A note that returns to its starting pitch
Approached by leap and left by step
questions.explain: A passing note connects two chord tones a third apart, approached and quitted by step in the same direction.
